executiveSummary: GM0917's 2025 identity, centre, population, 57 neighbourhoods, two BAG places, eight settlement labels, three stations and eight NWB-derived municipal-border links are coherent, and the complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. The named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel river preset assigns landlocked, elevated Heerlen direct inundation stress of 1.349871 at T+24 and T+72, up to 43,174 affected people-equivalent and 2,664,970.032 event-attributable deprived person-hours without selecting a Caumerbeek/Geleenbeek, rainfall, sewer, terrain or Waterschap Limburg event. That unsupported direct amplitude must be suppressed, while local brook, hillslope, groundwater and pluvial-drainage risk remains Unknown pending a governed event. Eight unrelated individual hazards reuse exactly the same complete 57-neighbourhood rank. A controlled ignition in Heksenberg ranks its containing neighbourhood 35th, and a controlled source at the coordinates of an observed preliminary M0.877542 KNMI event in Welten-Dorp ranks the containing neighbourhood seventh while generating 0.175227 g and 43,224 affected people-equivalent; this is a generic synthetic stress test, not a replay of the small observed event. Former-mine water rise, uplift, subsidence, sinkholes and possible microseismicity are distinct mechanisms and must not be conflated with tectonic shaking. Public water, wastewater, road, rail, transit, care, education, antenna, air-quality and grid-planning data improve context but do not establish live topology, occupancy, capacity, backup, incident state or restoration. The Dutch municipal graph also stops before the operational Heerlen-Parkstad-Aachen continuation. Every exact first-72-hour effect therefore remains an exercise output, and Unknown, NoData or zero matched records must never be rendered as zero or safe.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0917 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated source snapshot retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0917 as Heerlen and reports 87,522 residents, density 1,949/km², 24.8% aged 65 or older and 21,993 one-person households; the generated centre [5.961395629438655, 50.902066930271985] is inside the 2025 boundary.

Fifty-seven published neighbourhood rows in 23 districts sum to 87,515 residents, seven below the municipality total (-0.008%); households sum to 46,060 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 21,720. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 87,522 without rewriting the source rows.

BAG supplies two active woonplaatsen, Heerlen and Hoensbroek, and BRT supplies eight labels: one woonkern and seven deelkernen. BAG/PDOK place context is Public Domain Mark 1.0; CBS/BRT are edition-based CC BY 4.0. Labels are not water catchments, fire perimeters, mine zones or service areas.

Average home value and housing-tenure fields cover 51/57 neighbourhoods, cars per household 48/57, and benefit fields 53/57; district-heating share and public charging cover 0/57. Publisher null, suppression and non-applicability remain NoData, not zero. These annual resident statistics are context rather than incident-time occupancy or individual vulnerability.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — July 2021 regional water-system analysis, current maps/register and Hoensbroek rainwater-buffer project
evidenceSources.edition: July 2021 event analysis; current register inspected 3 September 2026; buffer announcement 9 July 2025
supports: The official retrospective reports an average 93 mm in two days in the Geleenbeek basin and locally up to 175 mm around Heerlen/Caumerbeek, extensive flooding and strong sensitivity to paved area. It explicitly says local pluvial mechanisms need separate study. This is historical analysis, not a live forecast or arbitrary T+72 forcing.

Waterschap Limburg's public maps expose water levels, groundwater, registered drainage and water assets. Its legger records design, ownership and maintenance context; it is not a complete event-time topology, telemetry feed, capacity statement or operating-state guarantee.

A planned approximately 1,300 m³ buffer under Raadhuisplein was announced for Hoensbroek to reduce sewer overload and benefit the Caumerbeek system. Project intent and nominal storage are not proof of completion, available incident-time volume, catchment connectivity or performance under the simulator's event.

The historical PDF and documentary pages publish no machine event contract or blanket operational cadence. Public web-map and register licences, native resolution, coverage and NoData must be retained per layer and verified before caching or redistribution; absent pixels/assets remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Heerlen / Provincie Limburg / Staatstoezicht op de Mijnen
evidenceSources.title: E03 — Former coal-mining effects, rising mine water and current geothermal oversight
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal and provincial pages inspected 3 September 2026; SodM permit advice 18 November 2025; I3ML programme from January 2026
supports: Heerlen states that stopped mine pumping allows mine water to rise, producing soil uplift and possible deeper-groundwater-quality effects, with decades before equilibrium; monitoring wells are used and residents report cracking or subsidence that may be mining-related. The I3ML investigation programme began in January 2026.

The Province identifies unstable old workings, mine-water recovery, ground movement and possible damage as continuing former-mining concerns following the 2011 't Loon event. Documentary risk recognition does not identify an incident, probability, deformation field or affected building.

SodM's 2025 Mijnwater permit advice says the existing Heerlen system uses former workings and separately describes subsidence, uplift, sinkholes and possible tremors near natural faults, requiring monitoring and action plans. It is regulatory/project context, not an observed municipal hazard surface.

These official pages have no common machine-readable event feed, declared spatial completeness or standard redistribution licence. Mine-water change, slow ground deformation, cavity/sinkhole formation, gas/groundwater effects and seismic ground motion must remain distinct evidence classes and cannot be inferred from one another.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Crisisplan 2024–2027, Limburg care-risk profile and draft renewed high-water response plan
evidenceSources.edition: Crisisplan 2024–2027; care-risk profile public in 2025; draft high-water plan consultation 15 July–26 August 2026
supports: The adopted regional crisis framework provides roles and coordination context for the first 72 hours; the care-risk profile identifies care-continuity and interdependency concerns. Neither document provides live activation, staffing, occupancy, acceptance, resources or restoration commitments.

The public 2026 high-water notice distinguishes the regional water system of streams/tributaries from the Maas and defence/polder mechanisms and proposes an impact team. The cited version was a consultation draft, not evidence that the plan was adopted, activated or applicable to a particular simulation clock.

Authority plans support explicit incident, owner, decision, resource, action and validity ledgers. They do not select a Caumerbeek/Geleenbeek hydrograph, determine neighbourhood depth or prove a road, hospital, pump or shelter state.

These public documents are planning evidence with policy-period/draft validity and no operational machine cadence or standard reuse licence found. They may support governance and exercise design only; missing live action remains Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — KNMI FDSN observed seismic catalogue and RIVM hourly air-quality and acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: KNMI rolling 365-day municipal-bbox query and RIVM context snapshots retrieved 2 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: The event-updated KNMI FDSN catalogue, CC BY 4.0 by default, returned one origin in GM0917: preliminary/manual event knmi2025spjd at 2025-09-22T13:18:26.699Z, magnitude 0.877542 MLs, depth 1 km, location Heerlen and coordinates [5.957, 50.876] within Welten-Dorp.

A hypocentre point and revisable magnitude are observed-event provenance, not a ShakeMap, future probability, continuous shaking field, building damage, mining attribution or service consequence. Zero events outside the returned scope would mean no covered catalogue record, not zero seismic hazard.

Two RIVM stations returned indicative hourly PM2.5 values for 2026-09-02T17:00Z: 3.38 µg/m³ at Heerlen-Looierstraat and 3.33 at Heerlen-Jamboreepad. The snapshot publishes no standard reuse licence in the consumed metadata and is neither a smoke plume nor a forecast aligned to the exercise clock.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 is a dated CC0 questionnaire release and identifies Zuyderland Heerlen as a 24/7 acute-care location with acute obstetrics, 24 treatment rooms and 38,500 visits reported for 2025. Register capacity and annual visits do not establish incident-time acceptance, beds, staff, backup, diversion or patient demand.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi / NDW / Stadsregio Parkstad Limburg
evidenceSources.title: E06 — NWB roads, rail stations, scheduled transit, current road context and Heerlen–Aachen regional continuity
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail/GTFS/NDW public snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026; Parkstad pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The monthly CC0 NWB input produces eight logical GM0917 border edges on A76, A79, N281, N300 and Laar to Beekdaelen, Kerkrade, Voerendaal, Brunssum and Simpelveld. Repeated sections are series/corridor provenance, not additive capacity, and nominal capacities of 150/260 are scenario units rather than measured throughput.

ProRail's CC0 register identifies Heerlen, Heerlen Woonboulevard and Hoensbroek stations; GTFS provides 101 stop areas. Static railway geometry, stations and scheduled-feed validity do not establish running service, passengers, accessible vehicles, evacuation capacity, response priority or restoration.

Parkstad describes Heerlen–Aachen as a cross-border daily urban system of more than 800,000 people and identifies mobility, energy and water dependencies; it separately documents the Heerlen–Landgraaf rail corridor and Aachen connection. The current municipal graph has no typed German continuation, border operations or mutual-aid state.

The CC0 NDW context assigned zero current situations to GM0917 at retrieval. That means no covered record matched the boundary and time, never that motorways, regional/local roads, crossings, rail or transit were open. NWB/ProRail are registers; GTFS is best-effort schedule context; NDW is timestamped situation context.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / RIVM / DUO / Rijksinspectie Digitale Infrastructuur / Netbeheer Nederland
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water-chain, care, education, antenna and electricity-planning context
evidenceSources.edition: Public context snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026; HWH contributor dates vary; RIVM acute care v1.1; NBNL planning snapshot current at retrieval
supports: Full CBS-boundary containment assigns 47 HWH public records to GM0917: RWZI Hoensbroek and 46 weirs. IMWA/DAMO is CC BY-SA 4.0 with provider-dependent update and completeness. Registration does not prove connected catchment, flow direction, compatible capacity, control, power/backup, operating state or recovery.

The context contains 67 DUO education locations and 131 RDI antenna records: 83 mobile, 15 fixed, one broadcasting, one other and 31 amateur. DUO is a daily CC-BY register; RDI's consumed service has no declared standard reuse licence or guaranteed cadence. Neither provides occupancy, shelter role, coverage, backhaul, traffic, power or backup.

One postcode-level NBNL sample identifies Enexis HUSK/Huskensweg: withdrawal 66.1 MW existing, 50.8 MW required, 11.9 MW queued/50 requests; injection 55.1 MW existing, 24.7 MW required, 5 MW queued/27 requests; TenneT categories 3/3 and ten projects, earliest 2028. It is planning context with partial spatial coverage and an unstated exact dataset licence, not local feeder topology, live load, outage, reserve or restoration.

RIVM care, DUO, RDI, HWH and NBNL records have affectsSimulation=false in the current context. Their source-specific versions, timestamps, licences, spatial coverage and NoData must remain visible; a record count or sampled postcode must not be promoted to municipal operational completeness.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — City-centre rainwater system, dated cooling-room offer and local nature/recreation context
evidenceSources.edition: Rainwater ordinance from December 2023; cooling-room notice 25 June 2026; pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The municipality documents city-centre soil/infiltration investigation and a rainwater system intended to reduce drainage/sewer overload under the December 2023 ordinance. Policy and design intent do not supply current inlet, pipe, storage, groundwater or pump state.

On 25 June 2026 Heerlen advertised named cooling rooms with location-specific opening hours. This proves a dated heat-response option only; it does not make a location an always-open shelter or guarantee staff, capacity, accessibility, cooling, backup or activation at another time.

Municipal visitor information places Heerlen between two stream valleys and lists nature/recreation routes and starts including Brunssummerheide and Terworm. This is geographic/visitor context, not an authoritative fuel polygon, ignition, occupancy count, access state or incident perimeter.

The pages have no stable machine event API, guaranteed refresh cadence, full spatial coverage or standard redistribution licence identified. Their simulation role is documented local mechanism and action context; unavailable live state remains Unknown.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across all eight services with complete finite output.
notes: Focused reproduction used MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0917 pnpm audit:model; one file and two tests passed over the complete 10 × 6 × 8 contract.

Peak checkpoint severity / maximum affected / T+72 event-attributable deprived person-hours are: severe storm 0.442221 / 6,079 / 361,710.032; pluvial 0.661939 / 23,255 / 1,006,486.423; river 0.426318 / 43,174 / 2,664,970.032; coastal 0.080081 / 0 / 386,523.043; heat 0.673916 / 6,834 / 591,251.359.

The standalone coastal preset has zero direct inundation but retains wind effects; the canonical earthquake is remote and wildfire has zero direct flame. numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, exact no-event behavior, local reconciliation, causal arithmetic and cumulative burden pass.
notes: All availability values stay in [0,1]; hazard dimensions, demand, delivery, affected people-equivalent and deprived person-hours remain finite and non-negative.
Zero-intensity scenarios return exactly zero severity, affected population and event-attributable deprived person-hours; repeated runs are deterministic and cumulative burden is monotone.

Every service allocates all 57 local rows and reconciles to 87,522 residents; local demand/delivery and headline totals close within floating-point tolerance, and map-layer selection does not alter the scenario state.
Passing arithmetic proves internal consistency only; it does not validate the event source, neighbourhood distribution, lifeline topology or operational precision.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A shared seeded rank and source-containment failures contradict Heerlen's mechanism-specific water, fire and seismic geography.
notes: At T+24 severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire share the exact full 57-neighbourhood order: Schrieversheide, Egstraat en omgeving, Heerlen-Centrum, Dr Schaepmanplein en omgeving and Giesenveld lead; Douve Weien is last.

A controlled T+11 ignition at the Heksenberg neighbourhood centre produces direct fire 0.635803, smoke 0.533561 and 22,203 affected people-equivalent, yet Heksenberg ranks 35th while the same generic five neighbourhoods lead. The point is a synthetic diagnostic, not a proven combustible feature or incident.

A controlled source at the observed KNMI coordinate in Welten-Dorp produces 0.175227 g and 43,224 affected people-equivalent at T+6, while Welten-Dorp ranks seventh. It deliberately exercises generic attenuation and does not replay the observed M0.877542 event.

A municipality-id seed cannot represent Caumerbeek/Geleenbeek runoff, local heat, fuel/smoke, an event ground-motion field and cyber system boundaries simultaneously; displayed hotspot precision is unsupported.

NWB links correctly function only as logical Mobility and explicitly assumed road-logistics Supply context; they are not power, drinking-water, wastewater, gas, telecom or hospital topology.

RWZI Hoensbroek/weirs, the 1,300 m³ buffer proposal, Enexis planning sample, antennas, Zuyderland and stations/stops supply context but no compatible connectivity, load/flow, outage, controls, backup, live capacity or repair state.
No typed Aachen continuation, alternate acute-care destination, wastewater catchment, supply depot or operator restoration route supports the exact service outcomes.

causalTrace.summary: Model ledgers close and public context remains non-causal, but source relevance and operational actions remain unsupported.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; ordered service-stage deltas close to availability; weighted service-loss contributions close to system pressure; local demand/delivery and municipality totals reconcile.
Preparedness/intervention stages change modeled consequences rather than hazard fragility, and official register/observation/planning layers remain affectsSimulation=false.

The trace does not select a Waterschap hydraulic event, mine-deformation or ground-motion field, fire perimeter, cyber system boundary, operator topology, care acceptance or first-72-hour authority action.
Arithmetic closure therefore supports explainability of the synthetic model, not source-valid local causation.

recovery72h.summary: Sustained-water gating is conservative, but precise deterioration and recovery lack event footprints, action owners and resources.
notes: River retains direct inundation stress 1.349871 from T+24 through T+72, affected people-equivalent grows from 40,710 to 43,174 and burden reaches 2,664,970.032 while service consequences persist without a selected local event.

Compound retains flood stress 0.709991 at T+72, affected grows from 52,193 to 55,419 and burden reaches 3,105,259.730 even as headline severity falls from 0.905330 at T+24 to 0.554102; exact service trajectories have no named operator action or resource.

The standing-water guard appropriately prevents generic restoration under persistent modeled water, but no footprint, recession/dewatering, accessible route, pump/crew/material/fuel, switching, patient diversion or completion state validates its local timing.
Every T+0/6/12/24/48/72 plateau, deterioration and restoration needs a typed driver/action/resource ledger with authority, issue/observation/valid time and uncertainty.

findings.summary: A generic earthquake stress test neither replays Heerlen's observed small event nor represents former-mine ground mechanisms.

Retain coastal direct water at zero only for the narrow standalone North-Sea screen, never as an all-flood or compound all-clear.

findings.summary: First-72-hour deterioration, plateau and restoration are not tied to named authority actions, resources or access.
findings.evidence: River and compound preserve unsupported standing water and increase affected people-equivalent through T+72; compound severity falls while system pressure rises from 0.563266 at T+24 to 0.589430 at T+72. Generic recovery fields do not name pump/dewatering, isolation/switching, inspection, clearance, repair, patient diversion, supply, crew, material, fuel, access or completion evidence.
findings.action: Require a typed incident/action/resource ledger at T+0/6/12/24/48/72: authority/owner, target, prerequisite, crew/material/fuel/water, route/access, start/end, state, issue/observation/valid time, evidence class, uncertainty and counterfactual. Unsupported automatic recovery stays synthetic and must not be attributed to an operator.

findings.summary: The complete deterministic numerical, causal, allocation and checkpoint contract passes for GM0917.
findings.evidence: The focused gate covers all ten presets, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and eight services. Outputs are finite/deterministic, zero-event behavior is exact, allocation and demand/delivery reconcile, causal ledgers close, burden is monotone, selected layers are invariant and sustained modeled water prevents premature generic restoration.
findings.action: Keep GM0917 and national ALL coverage in regression; add assertions for major-river suppression, local pluvial evidence support, hazard-rank independence, fire/quake source containment, mining separation, NoData, cross-border access and action-led recovery.

corrections.summary: Suppress unsupported GM0917 major-river precision and integrate governed local pluvial/fluvial pathways.
corrections.validation: Set direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel amplitude/exposure for GM0917 to unsupported/suppressed; do not convert this to flood-safe. Preferred local inputs are Waterschap Limburg's current separate pluvial/fluvial design-scenario products and water/groundwater/register services, the July 2021 event analysis for retrospective validation, KNMI event-valid rainfall, AHN terrain and governed municipal/WBL GWSW/catchment assets. Preserve publisher, layer/model edition, scenario/rainfall/hydrograph, issue/valid time, CRS, native resolution, units, footprint, arrival/recession, coverage, licence and NoData; official design scenarios are not observed T+0 water.

corrections.summary: Replace shared neighbourhood ranks and add source-contained local fire and seismic exercises.
corrections.validation: Require independent hazard-specific surfaces. For fire use IPO combustible-area geometry only as eligibility, event-valid KNMI weather and authority ignition/perimeter/fuel/access/suppression; a selected direct-fire source must lead its containing/intersecting cells unless the physical model documents otherwise. For seismic, use KNMI FDSN event revision plus station/ShakeMap or reviewed GMPE/site inputs; observed M0.877542 must not create the diagnostic 0.175227 g result. Preserve source time, uncertainty, licence and NoData, and suppress local ranks absent support.

corrections.summary: Create a distinct former-mining ground and mine-water pathway rather than conflating it with earthquake.
corrections.validation: Use Heerlen/Province/SodM/I3ML documentary and monitoring evidence in its native role; add BRO/NLOG or authorised deformation, shaft/working, groundwater/mine-water and building evidence only with publisher/version, measured quantity, spatial support, observation/valid time, coverage, licence and uncertainty. Separate slow uplift/subsidence, episodic sinkhole/cavity, groundwater/gas and seismic shaking. No selected/observed state remains Unknown and must not inherit a generic earthquake damage curve.

corrections.validation: Reconcile HWH's one RWZI/46 weirs and the planned Hoensbroek buffer against native municipal GWSW, WBL/Waterschap catchment, pipe, inlet, overflow, transport, pump, buffer and control data. For Enexis/WML/gas/telecom use authorised privacy/security-safe aggregate zones, outage and restoration ranges. Public HWH CC BY-SA records, NBNL sampled planning MW/queues, RDI points, DUO and provider territories retain contributor/sample coverage and affectsSimulation=false without verified topology, units, current state, backup and valid time.

corrections.summary: Add destination-aware Parkstad–Aachen mobility, care and supply continuity.
corrections.validation: Use monthly CC0 NWB, CC0 ProRail, feed-valid GTFS and timestamped CC0 NDW only in their proper road/rail/schedule/situation roles, supplemented by reviewed German/public border references and authorised operational state. Represent A76/A79/N281/N300, stations, onward Aachen links, Zuyderland/alternative care and supply/response destinations with country, direction, mode, one physical capacity ceiling, accessibility, emergency priority, authority, valid time and fallback. Missing NDW/GTFS records never mean open/operating.

corrections.summary: Evidence-gate other hazards and decision-facing UI precision municipality by municipality.
corrections.validation: Maintain a support matrix for hazard, neighbourhood surface and each service. Exact ranks, percentages and export require named event/source, publisher/version, issue/valid time, coverage, licence, NoData and uncertainty. Coastal zero is retained only for the narrow direct North-Sea source; local stream/pluvial/compound effects remain separate. KNMI/RIVM observations, warnings, registers, plans and synthetic outputs display distinct evidence classes.

corrections.summary: Make all first-72-hour recovery conditional on traceable actions, resources and access.
corrections.validation: At T+0/6/12/24/48/72 every deterioration, plateau and restoration cites driver, authority/owner, target, prerequisite, crew/material/fuel/water, route/access, start/end, state, issue/observation/valid time, evidence class and uncertainty. Retain conservative standing-water repair blocking only for selected exposed zones/assets. Dated cooling-room offers, plans and annual facility/register facts cannot become automatic completed actions or live capacity.

residualLimitations: This artifact audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a forecast, warning, evacuation instruction, hydraulic assessment, fire forecast, mine-safety determination, hospital status or operator restoration commitment.

CBS 2025 values are rounded, suppressed or unavailable and resident population excludes visitors, commuters, students, patients, staff, responders and displaced people; no authoritative timestamped occupancy is consumed.

Generalized municipality/neighbourhood geometry and centroids are not adequate for steep flow paths, sewer catchments, regional streams, mine workings, nature fuels, ground motion, building exposure, road crossings or service areas.

The July 2021 water analysis is retrospective and the Waterschap/municipal buffer and drainage pages are design/planning evidence. None is current T+0 water, completed protection, catchment capacity or arbitrary T+72 outcome.

Waterschap web maps and registers require layer-specific confirmation of licence, version, resolution, units, coverage and NoData before redistribution or causal use; a registered/realised asset does not prove operation, connectivity, capacity, backup or restoration.

KNMI event knmi2025spjd is a preliminary/manual observed catalogue record. It is not a future probability, ShakeMap, damage surface or mining attribution, and a bbox with no other events would not make Heerlen seismically safe.

Former-mine water rise, ground uplift/subsidence, cavities/sinkholes, groundwater/gas effects and seismic shaking operate on different time/physics scales. Public narrative evidence does not provide a complete live deformation or consequence field.

IPO/municipal nature context does not establish current fuel/moisture, ignition, perimeter, smoke, people, access, water supply, crews or suppression; the Heksenberg source is a synthetic diagnostic only.

NWB, ProRail, GTFS and NDW do not establish scenario-time road/rail/bus operation, border passability, emergency priority, evacuation/ambulance throughput or restoration. No matched NDW situation is not an open route.
The Parkstad cross-border page establishes strategic/daily-system context, not live German/Dutch resources, border coordination, mutual-aid dispatch, energy/water flows or capacity.
Zuyderland's RIVM questionnaire row, DUO schools and dated cooling rooms do not establish live occupancy, staffing, acceptance, shelter role, accessibility, backup, stocks or patient/supply transfer.

HWH, NBNL and RDI data are registers or planning samples, with partial/provider-dependent spatial completeness and some unstated reuse/cadence. They cannot establish physical connectivity, current load/pressure/coverage, outage, reserve or repair.
RIVM hourly PM2.5 points are timestamped indicative observations, not a continuous smoke plume or forecast; no local Waterinfo observation is no data, not zero water.

Complete electricity, gas, drinking-water, wastewater, telecom, care, supply and emergency-resource topology, live state, backup, stocks, crews and restoration may be unavailable or security-sensitive and remains Unknown or explicitly synthetic.

Exact hazard, neighbourhood, affected-population, service-availability, recovery and deprived-person-hour values are synthetic/derived exercise outputs until critical/high findings are corrected and authorities review a selected event; impacts beyond T+72 are outside this audit.
